How the U.S. “saved” Japan — and themselves in the process

The Japanese yen recently fell to a 40-year low — nearly 164 to the dollar. And for the first time since 1998, the U.S. stepped in itself to support the yen’s exchange rate.

But why would America even save someone else’s currency?

Because Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. government debt, with roughly $1.14 trillion in U.S. Treasuries. And that’s a real trap.

Because of the crisis, Japan spent $73 billion in the spring to support the yen. But it still fell. The question became: where do you get even more dollars? — Exactly, by dumping those same Treasuries.

But if they start doing that, yields on U.S. debt will shoot up. In other words, Japan’s problems suddenly become America’s problems.

And that’s when the U.S. came up with a workaround: Japan was given the ability to borrow the dollars it needed against its U.S. Treasuries — instead of selling them on the market.

And the U.S. itself, to support the yen, sold its euro reserves instead of dollars. So they strengthened the yen without weakening the dollar.

Formally, the U.S. was saving Japan and its currency. In reality, it was saving its own debt market, and with it, the stability of the entire dollar system.

When you owe the world trillions, a crisis for your creditor automatically becomes a crisis for you. And saving them is the only way to save yourself.

I never expected AI to say *this*.

You’d assume they’d have coded it otherwise.

Banks want to automatically block the accounts of Russians who deposit an amount higher than their monthly income through an ATM – they will have to justify the origin of the money with documents.

Sources in the banking sector claim that major banks have started testing stricter cash deposit verification. Algorithms will compare the deposited amount with the client's official income and their usual financial behavior. If a person earns 50 thousand rubles and then deposits 100 thousand in cash into the account, the transaction can automatically be flagged as high risk.

After such a signal, the bank can temporarily restrict some operations and request confirmation of the origin of the money. Purchase contracts, receipts, and other documents explaining the appearance of a large sum will be required. They particularly want to scrutinize cases where the cash amount significantly differs from the person's salary or previous transactions.

It will also become harder to bypass the system by splitting the amounts. According to sources, several deposits of 20-30 thousand rubles in a short period can be linked together by the algorithm and evaluated as one large operation. As a result, the checks may affect not only the gray market but also ordinary Russians who have kept money at home for years, received cash from relatives, or sold a car.

In Krasnodar supermarkets, there is already an option to pay with digital rubles, but according to regulations, the limit for digital rubles is 300 thousand rubles. You can never have more than this amount in your digital wallet. And in the event of the cancellation of cash and other forms of national currency, wages cannot exceed 300 thousand rubles.

Oh, and yes, the digital ruble will be voluntary, according to the Central Bank of Russia. Just like vaccines and the doomsday messenger.

📌 Rebase Tokens: Why Your Balance Can Change Without a Trade

Main Points
⏺ Some tokens automatically adjust holder balances through a rebase mechanism
⏺ Your token count can increase or decrease without a normal buy or sell
⏺ This post explains why “more tokens” doesn’t always mean “more money”

1️⃣ Core Idea — the protocol periodically recalculates balances, increasing or decreasing token amounts.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — to target a price, manage supply, or create a special monetary design.
3️⃣ The Trap — if your balance grows but price falls harder, you didn’t actually profit.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — exchanges, wallets, and DeFi protocols may not handle rebasing balances cleanly.
5️⃣ Practical Check — track your share of total supply, liquidity, and rebase rules, not just token count.

Final Thoughts

Rebase tokens change both price and quantity. Beginners see “more coins,” but the market prices real value.
